directions.whole_relationship: Two differently branching plants and two deliberate hands create a comparison by habit, scale and handling. The bright field is occupied by chunky printed plant/hand forms and their weight-bearing pots, not a passive information board. The left Title/body sequence can remain familiar while the image, letter voice and colour rhythm are markedly different.
directions.positive_direction: A vivid citron and aubergine ink world with restrained burnt-orange touch points. Hand-drawn lithographic contours, chunky flat plant masses, sparse directional hatching and precise overprinted silhouettes make a confident graphic illustration. Use real-looking plant habit and adult hands, with irregular but controlled drawn edges. The Title has generous bold Korean sans shape and decisiveness; regular body is sharply printed, separated from the image’s grain. A hand gently tests the scale of a compact upright plant while another supports the broad-leaf plant at the edge of its pot. Distinguish the two growing habits and keep hand/pot/stem contact readable. Make the choice feel active through reach and touch, without adding fake comparison labels, arrows, numbers or a cute shopping mascot. The image is an authored ink illustration, not a 3D clay pot or leaf wreath.
